title: Iteration 1 of my 3D space RTS, GHOST TRACK
author: _Fauxpaw
selftext:
In GHOST TRACK, you are the newly appointed head of Operational Intelligence for a major battlefleet, tasked by your Admiral with keeping order in the outer rim of our solar system. Hyper-capable machines have made fleet-wide wireless networks impossible to secure, so humanity devolved into crude, cassette-futurist hardware to maintain an air gap: CRTs, analogue video feeds, and narrowband radio.

What does this mean for you? It means information is slow and late. You could believe you're directing a group of Captains against an enemy far across the battlefield, only to realize it's been over three minutes since their last report. You were giving orders to their destroyed ships on your plot board.

Here's the premise of the game being designed:

**Belief vs the Spatial Truth**: There is one true state of the battle, and nobody gets to see all of it. Sensors give noisy clouds of info, every ship acts on its own picture, and yours is stitched together from your Captains' reports. Speaking of..

**Captains are capable and autonomous**: They're competent tacticians, all on their own, but they need your Fleet Picture to see the wider battle. You give orders and Target Packages; they plan how to tackle them, each with their own personality and quirks. Send them into a screaming hell and they may refuse.

..enemy Captains are the same.

**Information is physical**: Reports can be wrong, so you confirm it visually. Fly a camera drone too far from a laser or radio link and its footage turns choppy and slow. You and the enemy can mess with each other's information: fake signals, jamming, and more.

**Diegetic Gameplay and UI**: You (*usually*) sit in a physical room on a ship in the battle. On a good day that's multiple consoles and a huge patchboard of camera feeds. On a bad day you've evacuated, and you're directing the battle from a dinky backup laptop on a cargo barge.

\- - - - -

Anyways. This is very much the first iteration (*not even sound yet, sorry for the silent reel*). One mission is playable and the first Milestone is almost complete. Ship cameras, an expanded Alert Queue and rudimentary sounds are coming up next.

To keep the game from turning into pure spaghetti, Claude developed a clean simulation vs UI split: \`rules/\` has zero rendering or UI code, so the game can run headless and be written out as text for an AI to play it. \`screen/\`, the part for humans, is drawn on top.

Most of the workflow derives from using Matt Pocock's skills, which have been an organizational godsend and I can't recommend them enough. Keeping a decision record, supplied by Claude question cards, has been hugely important - along with a weekly automation to check consistency and ensure my decisions are being maintained. Oh, right, and we use Godot, which is awesome.

Simple labs [like this](https://claude.ai/artifact/Pi1T1J6uvGnmhB4zGPYPxe) (*this is a early first pass, not final*) have been *integral* to making sure myself and Claude both have a shared understanding of the spatial language of the game, such that its becoming one of my go-to tools.

I'd appreciate feedback, especially surrounding the UI, and a question:

Besides some unarmed drones, you never steer ships yourself directly; you instead give indirect orders that autonomous Captains claim. Does having such a lack of control sound fun or frustrating to you?
